title: Cyril and Methodius
hookLine: two Greek brothers invent an alphabet so Slavs can worship in their own tongue

lines: TEACH US IN OUR OWN LANGUAGE.
cards: A prince in Moravia, in the heart of Central Europe, sends a message to the emperor in Constantinople. His people have heard Christian teachers, he says, but in languages they don't understand.

Send us someone who can teach us in our own language. The emperor turns to two brothers from Thessalonica, a Greek city; in the old life of Methodius, he tells them people from Thessalonica speak Slavonic well.
Their names were Constantine and Methodius. Constantine is better known by the name he took as a monk at the end of his life: Cyril. There was one problem.

teach.h: A PRINCE ASKS FOR HIS OWN LANGUAGE.
teach.b: Our main sources are two old lives of the brothers, written in Slavonic by their followers.

teach.h: IN THE BEGINNING WAS THE WORD.
teach.b: The life of Constantine says that he prayed, then made the letters, and began to translate the gospel, starting with the opening of John: in the beginning was the Word. The new letters began with the Word.
Scholars call the alphabet he made Glagolitic. A later alphabet, built on Greek letters, came to carry Cyril's name: Cyrillic, still in use today. Not everyone was pleased.

In Venice, the life says, he met clergy who insisted that God may be worshiped only in three languages, Hebrew, Greek and Latin, the languages written on Christ's cross. Constantine answered with scripture.
Doesn't the rain fall on everyone? Doesn't the sun shine on all? He quoted the Psalms, in the King James words: "Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD."
He cited Paul, who would rather speak five words people understand than ten thousand in a tongue they don't.

teach.h: EVERY MAN IN OUR OWN TONGUE.
teach.b: And at Pentecost, in Acts, the crowd asks: "how hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born?" The brothers took that question as a commission. The road was hard.
After Cyril died, Methodius faced opposition and was even imprisoned. But the Slavonic worship they began lived on, and Church Slavonic is still prayed in some Orthodox churches today.
Orthodox and Catholic Christians both honor the brothers, sometimes called apostles to the Slavs.

how: Orthodox and Catholic Christians keep a feast of Saints Cyril and Methodius, and some Slavic Orthodox churches still worship in Church Slavonic, the language of worship that grew from the brothers' translations.

games.q: you're Constantine in Venice. clergy tell you only Hebrew, Greek and Latin are fit for worship. how do you answer?
o: agree, and teach the Slavs Latin.
answer with scripture: let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord.
games.why: he answered from the Psalms and from Paul: worship people can understand.

practice: A word in Cyrillic, the alphabet named for Cyril: slovo, which means word, the Word that was in the beginning; its letters sound like S, L, O, V, O, though the first looks like a C and the fourth like a B.

Say it slowly, SLO-vo, and trace the shapes in the air or on your palm. If you pray, let it carry you to the opening line of John; if you don't, notice how strange and ordinary it is to learn one word in someone else's script.
